newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- up 1/8 to 1/4, eyeing CPI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- up 1/8 to 1/4, eyeing CPI.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds gained about 1/8 to as much as 1/4 point in spots in light action Monday, as fixed income markets focused on Tuesday's inflation data.

Economists surveyed by Reuters said they expect the May Consumer Price Index, set for 0830 EDT release, to show a 0.2 percent rise both overall and at the core. Optimism about the report and its implication that inflation is tame also helped keep the Treasury market firmer Monday.
The government long bond was up 14/32 at 99-4/32 to push the yield down to 6.69 percent in late trading.
Despite historically rich levels for muni prices compared to Treasuries, traders said the market is holding up well and new issues are seeing strong demand.
Sales for this week were expected to total $4.3 billion in 160 deals, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings added up to $3.2 billion in 73 sales, the largest total this year, and on the competitive side, 87 sales totaling $1.1 billion were scheduled.
Tuesday's largest issue is expected to be an $89 million New York State Mortgage Agency deal through Lehman Brothers, although several larger issues were on the possible list.
Actively quoted issues on Monday included Dade County, Fla., water and sewer system FGIC 5-1/4s of 2026, which were bid down one basis point from last week at 5.47 percent.
Jefferson County, Ala., FGIC 5-3/4s of 2027 were bid at 101-3/8, up 1/8.
September municipal futures rose 9/32 to 118-3/32, while September Treasury futures rose 7/32 to 112-2/32. The MOB spread between the two contracts widened to 193 from 191 at the close on Friday.
